name: Autosomal Dominant Optic Atrophy 12

criteria.description: Bilateral, progressive optic atrophy with visual impairment
Heterozygous pathogenic variant in AFG3L2 gene
Cerebellar ataxia or cerebellar signs (e.g., dysarthria, gait ataxia)
Lower limb spasticity or pyramidal signs
Family history of autosomal dominant optic atrophy or related neurologic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Both major criteria are required. Minor or supportive features strengthen the diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing for AFG3L2 pathogenic variant in the context of compatible clinical features.

laboratory: No disease-specific laboratory abnormalities; mitochondrial function studies may show complex V deficiency in research settings
imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT): thinning of retinal nerve fiber layer
MRI brain: cerebellar atrophy (in some cases)

distinguishingFeatures: OPA1 classic form rarely has cerebellar or spastic features
Spasticity is predominant; optic atrophy may be absent or less severe
Overlap in gene (AFG3L2), but different clinical emphasis
Typically acute/subacute vision loss without cerebellar or spastic features

redFlags: Rapidly progressive vision loss with neurological symptoms
Family history of optic atrophy with cerebellar or pyramidal signs
references: Charif M et al. AFG3L2 mutations cause dominant optic atrophy and cerebellar ataxia. Brain. 2020;143(2):457-464.
Yu-Wai-Man P, Chinnery PF. Dominant optic atrophy: novel OPA1 mutations and revised diagnostic criteria. Brain. 2013;136(Pt 2):376-384.
commonPitfalls: Misattributing visual loss to OPA1-related disease without genetic confirmation
Overlooking subtle cerebellar or pyramidal signs in patients with optic atrophy
Assuming all optic atrophy with neurological features is mitochondrial or recessive
Failure to obtain family history spanning both vision and neurological symptoms

extendedDiscriminators.feature: Presence of cerebellar ataxia or spasticity in OPA12
Autosomal dominant inheritance and chronic progression in OPA12

ruleOutCriteria: Absence of AFG3L2 pathogenic variant on genetic testing
No evidence of optic atrophy on ophthalmological examination
Acute, unilateral vision loss (not typical for OPA12)
